resources.string: Explore six important considerations for designing applications that work well on mobile devices.
Mobile users interact through touch on a small screen instead of using a precise mouse and full-size keyboard.
Use large tap targets, simple gestures, and forms that require minimal typing.
Mobile screens vary in physical size, pixel density, and portrait or landscape orientation.
Create flexible layouts that remain readable when screen dimensions or orientation change.
A mobile application may be paused or stopped while memory, battery, and processing power are limited.
Preserve important state and avoid unnecessary background work or battery usage.
A phone can respond to information such as location, movement, connectivity, and time.
Use contextual information only when it provides a clear benefit and the user understands why it is needed.
People often use mobile applications in short sessions while distracted or moving between activities.
Make common tasks quick, show progress clearly, and let users resume interrupted work.
Phones contain personal information and can easily be lost, shared, or used on unsafe networks.
Collect only necessary data, protect sensitive information, and clearly explain privacy choices.
